title: How to write a German CV
description: The format German employers expect, what to include and leave out, and the details that matter for applicants from abroad.
html:
A German CV (Lebenslauf) is more structured and more factual than the CVs common in many other countries. Recruiters expect a specific layout, and a document that does not follow it looks careless even if the content is strong. Here is what the format looks like and how to fill it.

The format

One to two pages, in reverse chronological order, with clear section headings and a table-like layout: dates on the left, details on the right. No paragraphs of prose. A professional photo in the top corner is still common, although not required. The document ends with place, date and signature.

What to include

  • Personal details: name, address, phone, email, date of birth and nationality. Marital status is optional and increasingly left out.
  • Professional experience with employer, role, dates and three to five bullet points on responsibilities and results.
  • Education with institution, degree, dates and final grade.
  • Skills: languages with levels, software and technical skills.
  • Further training, certificates and, where relevant, publications.
  • Interests only if they say something about you.

What to leave out

Long personal statements, references on the CV itself, unexplained gaps, and anything not relevant to the role. Do not exaggerate language skills; they will be tested in the interview.

Quality over quantity

German recruiters read for precision. Numbers, named projects and concrete outcomes carry more weight than adjectives. A CV that has been adapted to the job description beats a generic one every time.

Applicants from abroad

State your visa status or right to work in a short line; employers appreciate knowing. If your degree is from outside Germany, add a line on its recognition status. Explain any unfamiliar institution in a few words. If you hold an Opportunity Card, say so; it tells the employer that you can start without sponsorship.

Cover letter and template

A cover letter (Anschreiben) usually accompanies the CV. It runs to one page and explains why this role, why this company and why you. Our free download includes CV and cover letter templates in German and English that follow the format described here.
